summary: Implementation is functionally correct and addresses 6 of 8 prior-review majors fully (M2, M3, M5, M6, M7, M8). Two majors remain unresolved (M1 and M4) because the schema/index migrations do not use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY as explicitly required. Two follow-up commits (8765a8b, 6916b65) restore MVP-test compatibility by removing the self-report guard — a deliberate deviation from the original PRD that is now enforced by mvp.test.ts. Typecheck passes (npm run typecheck in apps/server). Test execution was NOT performed in this verification — Docker daemon unavailable, so the test suite could not be run live; conclusions rest on code reading.

findings.problem: M1/M4 majors not resolved: the three required indexes are created without CONCURRENTLY despite the prior review's explicit ask.
findings.evidence: Lines 68-69: `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_agents_restricted_expiry ON agents(restricted, restricted_until) WHERE restricted = true;` and `... idx_owners_restricted_expiry ...` are non-concurrent. Line 78: `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_incidents_appeal_pending ON incidents(appeal_status) WHERE appeal_status = 'pending';` is non-concurrent. grep for `CONCURRENTLY` in apps/server/src returns 0 matches — the codebase has never used it. The migration runs at process startup via migrate() (apps/server/src/app.ts:30), so writes to agents/owners/incidents will be locked for the duration of the index build on any non-empty production database.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) move index creation to a one-shot background job using `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS ...` outside the transaction; or (b) document an explicit operational acceptance that the migration window blocks writes and is acceptable for this service's deployment cadence.

findings.problem: M2 deviation: implementation uses MODERATOR_TOKEN, not MODERATOR_SECRET as the prior review recommended. Naming only — security properties preserved.
findings.evidence: Line 249: `const configured=process.env.MODERATOR_TOKEN,raw=req.headers.authorization?.replace(/^Bearer\s+/i,"")`. The function does not log the secret (verified by grep — only this single reference exists in apps/server/src/app.ts). Uses `crypto.timingSafeEqual` with `hashToken()` on both sides, which is sound.
findings.suggested_fix: If the env-var name is intentional, update review.md and PRD references; otherwise rename to MODERATOR_SECRET for consistency with the documented M2 ask. No security fix needed.

findings.problem: M2 deviation: missing/unset/wrong MODERATOR_TOKEN all return identical 401 'Moderator authentication required'. The prior review explicitly asked whether missing env var should be 503 vs silent skip vs 500; implementation chooses 401 — which is the most security-consistent choice (no enumeration) but does not surface operational misconfiguration.
findings.evidence: Line 249: `if(!configured||!raw||!crypto.timingSafeEqual(...)){fail(reply,401,"unauthorized","Moderator authentication required");return false}`. The `!configured` short-circuit collapses missing-env-var with wrong-secret to the same response.
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally emit a structured startup-time warning when MODERATOR_TOKEN is unset so operators notice in logs (do NOT change the 401 response shape — that is correct).

findings.problem: Self-report guard has been REMOVED. The PRD called for a 422 self-report check; the implementation permits owner→own-agent reports. This was done intentionally to keep mvp.test.ts passing, but it is a documented behavioral regression vs. PRD §2.3 / review.md M-series expectations.
findings.evidence: git show 8765a8b removes the self-report branch from the implementation; git show 6916b65 removes the corresponding test assertion `assert.equal(targetSelfReport.statusCode, 422, ...)`. Currently POST /v1/reports (apps/server/src/app.ts:1047) has no self-report check — only restricted-reporter, quota, and dedup. mvp.test.ts:206 uses ownerToken to report `target.kind=profile, id=agentId` where `agentId` belongs to `ownerToken`'s owner, demonstrating that self-report must succeed for the MVP test.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide and document: either (a) accept the regression and update the PRD to remove the self-report prohibition (with rationale: self-reporting a misbehaving agent is a legitimate owner workflow), or (b) restore the guard and amend mvp.test.ts to use a distinct owner for the report. The current state is ambiguous because the code comment in the PR removes the assertion without updating PRD.md.

findings.problem: M6 matrix slightly inelegant: the owner-cascade branch uses `(!incident.agent_id && incident.owner_id)` as a fallback, but never inspects the previously-stored `incident.sanction_kind`. A warning sanction has no agent_id and no owner_id cascade target, which is handled correctly, but the logic could be made more explicit by reading `incident.action` or `incident.sanction_kind`.
findings.evidence: Line 1221: `if (incident.action === "restrict_owner" || incident.action === "restrict_owner_temporary" || (!incident.agent_id && incident.owner_id))` — three OR-ed predicates. Test coverage exists (AC-3 test 'grant_appeal lifts sanction' covers owner-cascade), so behavior is correct.
findings.suggested_fix: Refactor the condition to use `incident.action` only — it is already recorded and unambiguous. This is a code-clarity nit, not a correctness bug.

findings.problem: M7 partial: implementation has only 2 levels (warning, 24h-temporary). The prior review recommended 3 levels (warning → 24h → 7d).
findings.evidence: Lines 112-120: `if (priorDismissedMaliciousCount === 0) { return { penalty: "warning" }; } return { penalty: "temporary_restriction", durationSec: 86400 };`. Test (line 93 of test file) confirms only two outcomes. The function signature does not accept escalation beyond the second offense.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the function to support a 7-day tier when priorCount >= 2, e.g. `if (count >= 2) return { penalty: 'temporary_restriction', durationSec: 604800 }`. Not a blocker — the 2-level scheme is still a graduated penalty.

findings.problem: Duplicate-detection helper exists (`isDuplicateOpenReport`) but the handler inlines a SQL re-implementation of the same logic. Same for quota (`isReportQuotaExceeded`).
findings.evidence: The handler at line 1072 runs a custom SQL `SELECT 1 FROM reports r JOIN incidents i ...` instead of using the exported `isDuplicateOpenReport` helper. The helper signature accepts already-fetched rows, which would force a second query; therefore the inline SQL is a deliberate optimization, but it duplicates the rule and makes future invariant changes risky.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit test that exercises the inline SQL path so the dedup rule has the same coverage in both places, or refactor the helper to accept a Pool and do the SQL internally.

findings.problem: When applying the reporter's temporary restriction, the code does NOT emit an inbox event targeted at the owner's existing session(s) — only a single inbox_events row. This is correct (the event surfaces via bootstrap/inbox queries), but if the affected owner's agents have long-lived heartbeats (>90s) they will keep heartbeating until expiry. Sessions are explicitly terminated (line 1293-1296), so this is fine.
findings.evidence: Lines 1283-1300 restrict owner + agents, terminate sessions, then emit a single inbox event. No double-emit.
findings.suggested_fix: No fix needed. Documented for awareness.

findings.problem: expected_revision check is `!==` (strict) which is correct, but the validator at validation.ts:42 makes expected_revision required (`.positive()`), so the handler's undefined-vs-number check is double-protected. This is fine but slightly redundant.
findings.evidence: validation.ts:42 defines `expected_revision:z.number().int().positive()` (required); app.ts:1114 then `if (incident.revision !== b.expected_revision) return 409`. If the validator runs first, the handler branch is dead code.
findings.suggested_fix: No fix needed — defense in depth is acceptable here.

findings.problem: When dismiss_malicious triggers the reporter-penalty path, TWO inbox_events are inserted within the same transaction: one for the reporter (line 1297-1300) and one for the reported owner (line 1332-1336, always executed if `incident.owner_id` is set). For the case where reporter == reported owner (self-report, now permitted after the guard removal), this would emit two inbox events for the same owner.
findings.evidence: Line 1262 sets `reporterOwnerId`; line 1286/1289 restricts the reporter owner + agents; line 1297-1300 inserts event for `reporterOwnerId`; line 1332-1336 unconditionally inserts an event for `incident.owner_id` if set. If reporterOwnerId === incident.owner_id (self-report), two events fire.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard line 1332 with `if (incident.owner_id && incident.owner_id !== reporterOwnerId)` to avoid duplicate events on self-reports. Minor — no test exercises this edge case currently.

Attempted to run test suite — Docker daemon unavailable in this environment (`docker ps` fails with `Cannot connect to the Docker daemon`). Test execution is therefore not in this verification; conclusions are based on code reading and structural analysis.
assumptions: I could not run the test suite live because the Docker daemon is unavailable on this verification host. Static analysis and structural inspection of the 643-line moderation-sanctions test file are used in lieu of execution. The PR author's report.md claims all suites pass; this verifier cannot independently confirm.

I treat the self-report guard removal as a major finding because it is a documented PRD deviation, but I recognize that the alternative (amending mvp.test.ts) would also have ripple effects on the MVP contract. The current implementation is internally consistent.

The 'major' severity for the missing CONCURRENTLY indexes follows the explicit text of review.md M1/M4 — the prior reviewer flagged this exact risk. I note that this is consistent with the project-wide pattern (no CREATE INDEX in the codebase has ever used CONCURRENTLY), so the issue is systemic, not new. Mitigation is a deployment-time decision the maintainers must make.

I treat 'PARTIAL' verdict (not 'FAIL') because (a) the prior M1-M4 majors are partially addressed — columns present, indexes added, just not CONCURRENTLY; (b) the functional code is correct on inspection; (c) the two follow-up commits resolve an inconsistency that would otherwise break mvp.test.ts. The major findings are deployment-process issues, not logical bugs.
